questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): When talking about asking for item weight price (yesterday afternoon), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The cab driver'?

options.a: I am asking for item weight price right now.
options.b: Apples kg how much cost? yesterday
options.c: Apples kg how much cost?
options.d: How much are these organic apples per kilo?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "How much are these organic apples per kilo?".

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'iron out'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: Resolve minor problems or details in a plan.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
'iron out' means: resolve minor problems or details in a plan. Example: "We need one final sync to iron out contract details."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'touch base'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: Briefly connect with someone to exchange news.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'touch base' means: briefly connect with someone to exchange news. Example: "I will touch base with you after the review."

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'run errands'?

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 1 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.c: First problem root cause finding wanted.
options.d: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 2 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "సాయంత్రం మా ఇంటికి రండి, టీ తాగుదాం."
(Literal attempt: "Evening my house come, tea drink.")

options.a: Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together.
options.b: Evening my house come, tea drink.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I am needing to evening my house come, tea drink.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together."

Use 'drop by our home' for informal invitations.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 3 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.b: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 4 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.b: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.c: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.
